episode.title: Ep. 204 — Three years after the fall of Kabul

persons.name: Will Selber
persons.role: Co-host; retired USAF officer, Bulwark contributor, served at US Embassy Kabul in the final year; helped organize the Afghanistan United Front conference

mentions.quote: My co-host today is Will Selber... since retiring from the Air Force, has taken on a lot of responsibilities.

persons.name: Sami Sadat
persons.role: Former Afghan general; leader of the Afghanistan United Front, which organized the 15 Aug 2024 conference

mentions.quote: you played a role in putting that together with Sami Sadat's group, the Afghanistan United Front, which is one of the resistance groups that's organizing to take the fight to the Taliban

persons.name: Sara Harmouch
persons.role: Analyst who led the conference panel on the current situation in Afghanistan

mentions.quote: there was a second panel by Sara Harmouch, who and a couple of others who were kind of looking at the current situation in Afghanistan

persons.name: General Yazdani
persons.role: Former ANA corps commander in Kunduz, rotated out before the collapse; attended the conference

mentions.quote: one of them was General Yazdani, who was a former Corps commander up in Kunduz... he got rotated out right before the fall
he always said that they're going to come. The first, the real big problems will start up North.

persons.name: Javid Hamdard
persons.role: Former Afghan government official who spoke candidly about Afghan mistakes and corruption at the conference

mentions.quote: one of the speakers on my panel, Javid Hamdard... he served in the Afghan government in various capacities. And he was very honest about the mistakes

persons.name: Shuja Jamal
persons.role: Former Afghan Office of the National Security Council (international relations) official; author of 'The Decline and Fall of Republican Afghanistan'

mentions.quote: His name is Shuja Jamal. He was on the ONSC... He wrote a book called The Decline and Fall of the Republic of Afghanistan

persons.name: Mike Pompeo
persons.role: US Secretary of State who per Shuja Jamal pressured Ghani to release 5,000 Taliban prisoners by threatening to cut military assistance

mentions.quote: the amount of pressure like specifically from Mike Pompeo, Secretary of State Pompeo, in the form of military assistance. They were just going to cut it off.

persons.name: Ashraf Ghani
persons.role: Former Afghan president; released prisoners hoping to curry favor with the Trump administration; rotated commanders constantly; 'coup-proof'

mentions.quote: Ghani thought that it would curry favor with them... he would get favor from the Trump administration
Ghani was just going through corps commanders and police chiefs. And it was just like this constant rotation.
I just was waiting for an Afghan to step up and overthrow Ghani... they said that he basically coup proof.

persons.name: Hamdullah Mohib
persons.role: Afghan National Security Advisor under Ghani; part of the 'vipers' nest' rivalry in the final year

mentions.quote: this competing, like, real, like, Vipers Nest inside the Ghani administration between Ghani and his national security advisor, Hamdullah Mohib, and Yasin Zia and some of the ministers of interior

persons.name: Asadullah Khalid
persons.role: Afghan Minister of Defense in the final year, absent for medical treatment (Qatar) after earlier suicide-blast injuries; allegedly kept in post at US insistence

mentions.quote: Asadullah Khalid was the Minister of Defense... he was in a hospital in the Middle East
Asadullah Khalid was a minister of defense. He had sustained injuries, I think, when he was a governor from a suicide blast.

persons.name: Yasin Zia
persons.role: Afghan Chief of General Staff, dual-hatted as acting defense minister for most of the final year

mentions.quote: in his place was for the majority of the year was Dr. Yasin Zia, who was the chief of the general staff

persons.name: Sohrab Azimi
persons.role: Afghan commando officer whose team was overrun and who was executed on film by the Taliban in southern Afghanistan, ~June 2021
persons.status_detail: executed by the Taliban after his commando team was overrun, approx June 2021

mentions.quote: It started with Sohrab Azimi. That's when I knew, Bill, it was over when they killed him in southern Afghanistan... him and his team were overrun. And then the Taliban executed him and filmed it.

persons.name: Naqib Mirzada
persons.role: Afghan major, third Afghan West Point graduate, Ranger School; opening conference speaker

mentions.quote: Naqib Mirzada, who's a major... he's the third Afghan to ever graduate from West Point. He went to Ranger School.

persons.name: Hibatullah Alizai
persons.role: Afghan general who rose late in the war; son of a police intelligence director advised by Selber

mentions.quote: guys like General Hibatullah Alizai, right? I advised his father. I was his father's advisor at the Director of Police Intelligence for a year.

persons.name: Mustafa Wardak
persons.role: Afghan officer, graduate of the US Army School of Advanced Military Studies

mentions.quote: guys like Mustafa Wardak, who was a SAMS graduate, School of Advanced Military Studies

persons.name: Abdullah Abdullah
persons.role: Ghani's electoral rival whose dispute the US mediated

mentions.quote: we had to intervene with his conflict with Abdullah Abdullah during the last election

persons.name: Abdul Ghani Baradar
persons.role: Senior Taliban leader, now a deputy in the Taliban government (hosts: deputy for economic/foreign affairs); impersonated in 2010 by a Pakistani man who received US cash

mentions.quote: they found this guy in Pakistan, who they believe was Mullah Baradar... he's now like one of the Taliban, like the third deputy or second deputy minister... And they threw hundreds of thousands of dollars of this guy, but it wasn't him.

persons.name: Mullah Omar
persons.role: Taliban founder whose death was concealed for two years, nearly fracturing the movement

mentions.quote: covering up... the death of Mullah Omar and holding them up for two years, putting out statements in his name. They almost fractured because of it

persons.name: Lloyd Austin
persons.role: US Secretary of Defense; marked 'conclusion' of the Afghan war

mentions.quote: Secretary of Defense Austin... when he said it was the one-year anniversary of the conclusion of the Afghan War

persons.name: Mark Milley
persons.role: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs who said 'in a broader strategic sense, we lost'

mentions.quote: when General Milley said in a broader strategic sense, we lost

persons.name: Hamid Karzai
persons.role: Former Afghan president, 'our guy' installed by the US

mentions.quote: where I'm always happy to criticize Ghani and Karzai, and I just always remind everybody, those were our guys.

persons.name: Barack Obama
persons.role: Former US President; reversed planned Afghan withdrawal after Iraq lesson

mentions.quote: when Obama finally realized that he couldn't pull out... He learned his lesson in Iraq.

persons.name: Joe Biden
persons.role: US President who ordered the 2021 withdrawal, originally dated for 11 Sep 2021

mentions.quote: Why did President Biden withdraw?
the original withdrawal date was September 11th... 20 years to the day of 9-11

events.description: Afghanistan United Front conference on the third anniversary of the fall of Kabul; panels on past (Roggio), present (Harmouch) and future (Selber); attended by former ANA officers including Gen. Yazdani and Maj. Mirzada.
Fall of Kabul to the Taliban.
Doha Agreement signed without the Afghan government; led to hedging across Afghan forces; 'second to last nail in the coffin'.
Afghan government released 5,000 Taliban prisoners under US (Pompeo) pressure, who returned to the battlefield.
US withdrawal announced with original completion date of 11 September 2021.
Commando officer Sohrab Azimi's team overrun in southern Afghanistan; Taliban executed him on film.
Taliban assassination campaign targeting ANSF, Afghan Air Force pilots and their families during the 'reduction in violence'.
Taliban concealed Mullah Omar's death for two years, issuing statements in his name; near-fracture of the movement.
US paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to a man in Pakistan believed to be Mullah Baradar for peace talks; he was an impostor (NYT report).
Afghan commandos used to retake and hold district centers, repeatedly overrun; Roggio's point of knowing the war was lost (2017-19).
Secretary Austin marked the one-year 'conclusion' of the Afghan war; Gen. Milley said 'in a broader strategic sense, we lost'.

New York Times report on the 2010 Mullah Baradar impostor
Selber (with his mother), War on the Rocks article on moral injury
key_claims: The Taliban won through unity, persistence and willingness to take casualties, while expertly dividing the Afghan government and forces; the Afghan resistance's biggest challenge is unity.
The Doha Agreement was the second-to-last nail in the coffin and the withdrawal order the last; the 5,000-prisoner release was forced by Pompeo and accepted by Ghani hoping for US favor.
The Taliban's 'reduction in violence' was in practice an assassination campaign against ANSF, pilots and their families.
Leadership dysfunction in Ghani's final year (absent defense minister Khalid, dual-hatted Yasin Zia, Mohib rivalries, constant commander rotation) accelerated collapse; Ghani was 'coup-proof'.
Over 70,000 Afghan security personnel died, 3,000+ in the last year; the 'Afghans didn't fight' narrative is false.
US general officers have not admitted the war was lost, causing moral injury among veterans; the US lacks accountability and institutional learning.
